test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a key feature of offsprings produced through vegetative propagation?

options.text: They are genetically diverse from the parent plant.
They always grow slower than seed-grown plants.
They are genetically identical to the parent plant.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They are genetically identical to the parent plant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Vegetative propagation** is a type of **asexual reproduction** where new plants are produced from vegetative parts of the parent plant, such as **roots, stems, and leaves**.
 
• Since only **one parent** is involved and there is no fusion of gametes, the offspring produced are **genetically identical** to the parent plant. These identical individuals are often referred to as **clones**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• In this process, the cells divide through **mitosis** rather than **meiosis**. Because meiosis and **genetic recombination** do not occur, there is no **genetic diversity** among the offspring. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Vegetative propagation does not involve **pollen** or **ovules**, meaning it **does not require fertilization** to develop new individuals. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
